description: Extend parse_number(value) to implement the complete finite locale-number contract below. Return a float or None; do not change tests or the public function.
requirements: Accept int and float inputs except booleans. Return None for None, unsupported input types, nonfinite values, or numeric overflow.
For strings, strip surrounding whitespace and remove ordinary spaces, apostrophes, NBSP U+00A0 and narrow NBSP U+202F as grouping marks.

A string with only one punctuation kind accepts an optional sign, ASCII digits, and optionally one dot or comma followed by digits. A single separator is decimal: both '1.000' and '1,000' mean 1.0. Multiple same-kind separators are invalid.

When both dot and comma occur, the rightmost kind is decimal. The integer part must have a first group of 1 to 3 digits followed by one or more exactly 3-digit groups separated by the other kind; the fractional part must contain one or more ASCII digits. Optional leading sign is allowed.
Reject exponent notation, empty strings, partial numbers such as '.5' or '5.', NaN and infinity spellings, and malformed grouping. Never return a nonfinite float.

provenance.description: Numeric coercion is a real concern in the previously studied document-processing task pool; this expanded grammar and every implementation/test here are newly constructed, not a mined historical fix.

validity_limits: Calibration only; these tasks do not establish representative development performance or generality.
Hidden tests are independent of the solving run, not independently authored from this fixture's reference implementation.
The oracle is one valid implementation, not an exact patch requirement; behavioral alternatives are allowed.
Passing visible tests is intentionally insufficient. Base failure is seeded and does not predict model failure rate.
